title: Pull the spacer dowels and bond the laminate to the drawer front
instruction: Pull out the three spacer dowels so the laminate sheet bonds flat to the drawer front, still overhanging every edge.
context: Gluing plastic laminate onto a drawer front or countertop with contact cement is a familiar home-improvement and cabinetmaking job: contact cement is spread on both surfaces and left to dry, and because it grabs on first touch the sheet is first laid on spacer dowels and lined up; the dowels are then pulled so the sheet settles and bonds while still overhanging every edge for flush trimming.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m). A fixed MDF drawer-front blank, 160 (x) x 240 (y) x 18 mm, centred at x 0.30 m, y 0.0 m (top at z 0.7655 m, colour 0.50, 0.36, 0.24), its top face coated with dry contact cement. Three loose 12 mm round birch spacer dowels (24-sided prisms, dowel.obj, 300 mm long along y, 60 g, colour 0.86, 0.72, 0.50) lie on the blank at x 0.241, 0.300 and 0.359 m, running from y -0.17 to +0.13 m, so each sticks 50 mm out past the blank's -y edge. On them lies a grey-blue laminate sheet (colour 0.45, 0.55, 0.65) cut oversize to 176 x 260 mm: three 58 x 260 x 4 mm panels (panel_n, panel_m, panel_f at x 0.241, 0.300, 0.359 m, 40 g each, 1 mm apart) joined along y by two spring hinges (0.004 N m/rad toward flat, 0.002 N m s/rad damping, +-60 deg), with its underside 12 mm above the blank. The sheet overhangs the blank by 8 mm on each x edge and 10 mm on each y edge. Nothing else is on the table. Real world: the blank is an 18 mm MDF board cut to 160 x 240 mm; the sheet is 0.7 mm vertical-grade high-pressure decorative laminate cut to 176 x 260 mm, with two pencil ticks on each 260 mm edge, 59 and 117 mm from its near edge, dividing it into three 58 mm bands (near, middle, far) that match the simulated panels. Contact cement is applied to both mating surfaces, the blank's top face and the laminate's underside, following the cement maker's instructions, and left until dry to the touch and still within its open time when the trial starts. The dowels are uncoated.
scoring: Bonding: a panel bonds the first control step that its lowest corner is within 1 mm of the blank's top and it is within 3 deg of flat; from then on a fixed joint holds it where it lies for the rest of the trial. The sheet is registered when every panel's centre is within 6.0 mm in x and 8.0 mm in y of its set position, so the sheet still overhangs every edge of the blank by at least 2 mm. A panel counts when it is bonded, the sheet is registered, and both grippers' tool centre points are at least 3 cm from every point of the panel (released). Score (SCORE_OVER = 'end') = (number of counting panels) / 3. Success is all three panels counting, held for 1 s. Distance = the sum over unbonded panels of the lowest corner's height above the blank (m), plus how far (m) the worst panel is outside the registration window. Real world, checked after the run without lifting the sheet, for each band: released (no gripper touching the sheet, end photo); bonded flat (a 0.25 mm feeler gauge slid between laminate and blank at each place the band crosses the blank's edge goes in no more than 5 mm, and a 1 mm feeler gauge does not pass under a steel straightedge laid along the band's centre line); registered (a ruler shows the sheet overhangs the blank by at least 2 mm at both ends of every band and along the near and far edges). Score = bands meeting all three / 3. A band that touches the cement at an angle bonds where it touched; it is scored by the same checks, so a tilted touchdown that leaves a raised edge, a bubble or a shifted sheet loses that band's credit.
fidelity: The 0.7 mm laminate sheet is three rigid 4 mm panels joined by soft spring hinges along the dowels, so it bends only along y. Contact cement is a rule, not adhesion physics: a fixed joint switched on at first flat contact within 1 mm, so a tilted touchdown, which bonds at once on a real sheet, is more forgiving here. The blank is one fixed box. The dowel order is not scored, since shops differ (middle out or from one end).
reset_notes: The bond is permanent: each real trial uses a fresh blank and a fresh laminate sheet, both cemented as in the setup. In simulation the bonds clear at reset.
